subject: Encryption ownership & handover: follow-up and questionnaire
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novaclinics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Encryption ownership & handover: follow-up and questionnaire

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have agreement on owners and deliverables: 

Key takeaways:
- NovaClinics requires HIPAA coverage and GDPR scope for EU patient records; SOC 2 Type II in progress (target Q3).
- Primary questions center on key ownership model, support for customer-managed keys (BYOK), and options for HSM-backed KMS integration.
- You asked for a short mapping of at-rest vs in-transit encryption responsibilities and where Redwood would optionally host CMKs vs customers' KMS.

Action items / owners:
1) Redwood (Karthik + Marissa): provide concise answers for the questionnaire items around KMS/HSM, key rotation, key destruction, and audit logs. Deliverable: spreadsheet + narrative (attached draft). Due: Tue 2026-04-13 EOD.
2) NovaClinics (Daniel + security_ops): confirm whether you need HSM on-prem (SKD/HSM appliance) vs cloud-KMS import/externally-controlled key policies; share vendor questionnaire PDF. Due: Mon 2026-04-12.
3) Joint: schedule a short follow-up to walk the BYOK PoC plan and discuss performance/latency implications. Proposed slots: Wed 04/14 10–11am PT or Thu 04/15 2–3pm PT.

Short clarifications to include in our deliverable (we'll answer these explicitly in the attached spreadsheet):
- At-rest encryption: AES-256 with per-customer keys, wrapped by a KMS. Options: Redwood-managed KMS (default) or customer-managed CMKs (BYOK).
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 recommended) for all API and inter-service traffic.
- HSM options: we support HSM-backed Cloud KMS providers and have a documented BYOK import path for customer keys (support for external key references via KMS API).
- Key rotation: rolling rotation patterns supported; rotation without replay issues for cached KV/embedding flows described in answer doc.

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire_NovaClinics.pdf (placeholder you mentioned in the call), draft encrypted answers spreadsheet attached as encryption_answers_v1.xlsx.

Will get the first draft to you and security_ops by Tue EOD. If any of the owners above should be changed, let me know.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novaclinics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@novaclinics.com
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption ownership & handover: follow-up and questionnaire

Karthik — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side before you finalize the spreadsheet:

1) SOC 2: we are collecting SOC 2 artifacts; the timeline is Q3 but we need specific evidence around key lifecycle and access controls for ePHI.
2) HIPAA: yes, PHI scope includes event logs and generated outputs. We need confirmation that Redwood can sign a BAA and that the customer-managed key option keeps the key material under our control (i.e., Redwood never has plaintext access to CMKs).
3) HSM: we prefer HSM-backed keys. Initially cloud-HSM is acceptable (we use AWS CloudHSM), but we want to understand import/export limitations and whether Redwood supports a 'bring-your-key' that stays in our HSM with a remote reference.

I've attached the vendor questionnaire we typically send to vendors (vendor_security_questionnaire_NovaClinics.pdf). There are specific fields on key escrow, dual-control, and key deletion that will be important.

If you can call out where Redwood would need access (audit logs, key access requests) vs what stays in our control, that will speed legal/security reviews. Also, include sample rotation windows and any downtime or cache invalidation impacts we should expect during rotation.

We can do the Wed 04/14 10am PT slot for the follow-up. Please send a calendar invite with the agenda.

Regards,
Daniel Park
Head of Security Operations
NovaClinics

- Compliance mapping (SOC 2 artifacts, BAA language summary, audit log export): Sergio (owner).

Attachments to include in the bundle: encryption_answers_v1.xlsx (draft), byok-poc-plan.md (PoC checklist + infra diagrams). I've stubbed answers for the easy items. Stephanie/Sergio — please add detailed notes inline in the spreadsheet and mark items that require engineering or legal.

Deadline: Tue 2026-04-13 5pm PT so Karthik can send before EOD. If blocked on legal text for BAA or specific AWS CloudHSM behaviors, escalate to Legal with a note and I'll coordinate.

Subject: Re: Encryption ownership & handover: follow-up and questionnaire

Daniel — attaching the completed draft answers and a short BYOK PoC plan. Key highlights called out at the top of the spreadsheet and summarized below.

Summary (short):
- BAA: Redwood can execute a BAA; legal will provide standard language and we can add minor concessions for audit rights.
- CMK semantics: Customer-managed keys are supported. Redwood never retains plaintext of CMKs when BYOK is enabled; we accept KMS key references or imported wrapped keys depending on provider.
- HSM support: We support cloud HSM providers (AWS CloudHSM, Google Cloud HSM) for HSM-backed CMKs. For strictly on-prem HSM appliances, we offer a hybrid remote-key-reference model; engineering will validate latency with your infra during PoC.
- Rotation & cache: Rolling rotation supported; cache invalidation is handled via prefix-versioned KV keys — short-lived cache TTLs recommended for sensitive workloads. See the attached PoC plan for test cases.

Attachments: encryption_answers_v1.xlsx (detailed Q/A), byok-poc-plan.md (PoC steps, infra checks, perf tests). Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-encryption-answers

Next steps:
- We confirmed the follow-up call Wed 2026-04-14 10:00am PT. Calendar invite sent.
- If you want a short technical contact during the PoC, Stephanie will be the primary. Sergio will support compliance requests.

If this alignment looks good I'll mark the questionnaire as "answered (draft)" and we can iterate during the follow-up.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
